transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m stuck in this loop of double- and triple-checking my work for hours, and I can’t move on even when I know it’s already done right. It’s incredibly exhausting, and I just don't know how to break out of it.
Do you experience these persistent thoughts as intrusive, unwanted images or ideas that you feel forced to check, or are you primarily focused on the repetitive physical act of checking itself?

It is definitely the intrusive thoughts and vivid images that drive the whole thing. I get these sudden, terrifying flashes of a server getting hacked or my nephew getting hurt, and the constant "what if" loops create so much anxiety that I feel forced into the physical checking. I end up rereading code or jiggling door handles over and over just to prevent some catastrophe that I feel would be my fault.

When you are performing these repetitive checking behaviors, are you doing them primarily to neutralize the anxiety caused by your intrusive thoughts, or do you feel a need to perform these actions according to rigid, specific rules to make things feel 'just right'?

It’s actually a combination of both. The terrifying thoughts about a hack or my nephew getting hurt create an overwhelming anxiety that I desperately need to quiet down. But to get any relief, I feel forced to repeat the checking rituals in a very specific way until it finally feels "just right," otherwise I'm convinced something catastrophic will happen.

latest_inference.note: The patient describes a combination of obsessional thoughts (intrusive images of harm) and compulsive behaviors (checking rituals) performed both to neutralize anxiety and to achieve a 'just right' feeling. This presentation of mixed obsessions and compulsions aligns best with F42.2 (Mixed obsessional thoughts and acts), whereas F42.0 and F42.1 focus more exclusively on either thoughts or acts respectively.
